result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use bpmn:task for atomic work when the execution mode is unspecified. A task contains no internal flow.

Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.
Use end events for terminal outcomes. An end event has no outgoing sequence flow and is not the target of a message flow.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.

result.rule: When the description names an activity with a verb and an object, and a nearby clause or parenthetical adds a modifier to that object (a selection, a state, a milestone, a purpose, or an urgency), while the activity's own verb is stated in the text: Label the task with the verb and object exactly as the description states them, keeping the description's own wording. Do not add the modifier to the label, and do not swap the stated verb for a near-synonym that names a different act or outcome. Keep the modifier in a text annotation attached to the task.

When the description names an activity and attaches to it measurements, dimensions, criteria or qualifying conditions that the item must meet, as a separate clause or parenthetical: Label the task with the bare verb and object that the description gives for that activity, and leave the measurements, dimensions, criteria and conditions out of the label. Keep them in a text annotation attached to that task. Model a separate activity only when the description states a distinct action.

When the description states an activity whose verb is qualified by a quantity or frequency constraint (for example a minimum count or a repetition per period) that belongs to that same activity: Name the task with the verb the description uses for that act and keep the quantity or frequency wording that constrains it, in the description's language. Do not drop the constraint to shorten the label, and do not replace the stated verb with a synonym that names a different act or outcome, such as a removal verb where the description states a change of state.

When the description attaches a purpose, means, or recipient phrase to a described action (for example 'to ...', 'with additional ...', or 'to <party>' after the verb and object): Label the task with the main verb and object of the stated action only, and leave the purpose, means, or recipient phrase out of the label. Keep the wording close to the description's verb and object, so the label stays faithful and short.
